'''Dennis John Trewin''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AO}} FASSA is an Australian former public servant, who was the [[Australian Statistician]], the head of the [[Australian Bureau of Statistics]], between July 2000 and January 2007.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.theage.com.au/news/business/mining-boom-fails-to-deliver/2006/09/01/1156817098307.html | title = Mining boom fails to deliver | work = [[The Age]] | author = Tim Colebatch | date = 2006-09-02 | accessdate = 2007-01-31 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/D3110129.NSF/f128006d2d1e7c10ca2566fd0081ba4b/abbe75f1a0d205feca25722c001003ca!OpenDocument#AUSTRALIAN%20STATISTICIAN%20DENNIS%20TR | title = Statistical News Tasmania: Australian Statistician Dennis Trewin Retires |date=November 2006 | work = Newsletter, [[Australian Bureau of Statistics]] | accessdate = 2007-01-31}}</ref>

Trewin joined the ABS in 1966 as a statistics cadet.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://abs.gov.au/websitedbs/d3310114.nsf/4a256353001af3ed4b2562bb00121564/a0209509ae816da9ca25718c000c7adf!OpenDocument | title = Senior Staff Biographies - Dennis Trewin, Australian Statistician | work = [[Australian Bureau of Statistics]] | accessdate = 2007-01-31 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727121531/http://abs.gov.au/websitedbs/d3310114.nsf/4a256353001af3ed4b2562bb00121564/a0209509ae816da9ca25718c000c7adf!OpenDocument |archivedate=27 July 2011}}</ref>  Between 1992 and 1995 he was the Deputy Government Statistician in [[Statistics New Zealand]]<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.obs-pascal.com/docs.php?doc=53 | title = Biography for Dennis Trewin | work = Observatory Pascal | year = 2004 | accessdate = 2007-01-31 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20051216230924/http://www.obs-pascal.com/docs.php?doc=53 | archive-date = 16 December 2005 | url-status = dead }}</ref> and a Deputy Australian Statistician from 1995 to 2000, when he was appointed as the Australian Statistician.<ref name="oecd">{{cite web | url = http://www.oecd.org/speaker/0,2879,en_21571361_31834434_33630521_1_1_1_1,00.html | title = Speaker profile: Dennis Trewin | work = [[OECD]] |date=November 2004 | accessdate = 2006-06-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204041141/http://www.oecd.org/speaker/0,2879,en_21571361_31834434_33630521_1_1_1_1,00.html| archive-date=4 Feb 2012}}</ref>

Trewin was the driving force behind the ABS's pioneering 'Measures of Australia's Progress' (MAP), a new system of integrated national progress measurement, linking economic, social, environmental and governance dimensions of progress, a project which gained wide respect among other national statistical offices and helped bring about the OECD's global project, 'Measuring the Progress of Societies'.

He held other senior appointments in Australia such as non-judicial member of the [[Australian Electoral Commission]], a Director of the Australian Institute for Health and Welfare, a Commissioner for an Inquiry into the Not-for-Profit sector for the [[Productivity Commission]], a Council member of the [[University of Canberra]], a Trustee and Board member for ARIA (the superannuation funds for Commonwealth Government employees, Chair of the [[Australian Mathematics Trust]]{{citation needed|date=March 2026}} and an adjunct professor at [[Swinburne University of Technology|Swinburne University]] and the University of Canberra.  He has held the office of president of the [[Statistical Society of Australia]].<ref name="oecd"/>{{failed verification|date=March 2026}} He was elected a Life Member.

Internationally, in 2003 he completed a term as president of the [[International Statistical Institute]] having previously been vice-president and president of the [[International Association of Survey Statisticians]].  He is a past editor of the [[International Statistical Review]].<ref name="oecd"/>

He was chairman of the global executive board at the [[World Bank]], chairman of the Asia/Pacific Committee of Statistics, and chairman of the advisory board of Swinburne University of Technology's [[Swinburne Institute for Social Research]].<ref name="oecd" />

Trewin holds honorary life memberships of the International Statistical Institute and the Statistical Society of Australia.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://demography.anu.edu.au/Seminars&Lectures/ASEP_lectures_pdf/Trewin.pdf | title = The Australian & The Scanlon Foundation presenter profile: Dennis Trewin | work = College of Arts & Social Sciences, [[Australian National University]] | accessdate = 2007-01-31|format=PDF}}</ref> He was listed as one of Australia's Smart 100 in a 2003 poll run by the Australian magazine ''[[The Bulletin (Australian periodical)|The Bulletin]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | url = http://bulletin.ninemsn.com.au/bulletin/site/webAllArticles/93395FB0469ED912CA256DAF002C2CFC | title = The Bulletin Smart 100 | journal = [[The Bulletin (Australian periodical)|The Bulletin]] | format = broken link | accessdate = 2006-06-25 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060621082754/http://bulletin.ninemsn.com.au/bulletin/site/webAllArticles/93395FB0469ED912CA256DAF002C2CFC | archive-date = 21 June 2006 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He received an Honorary Doctorate from James Cook University in 2015.

He was elected as a Fellow of the [[Academy of Social Sciences]] and was Chair of its Policy and Advocacy Committee.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} In 2007, he was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] (AO)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/lookup/media%20release | title=Bureau Executives Honoured in Queen's Birthday List | publisher=[[Australian Bureau of Statistics]] | date=12 June 2007 | accessdate=18 November 2024}}</ref> and received a Centenary Medal{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} in Recognition of his services to Australian and international statistics. He was elected to the Alumni Hall of Fame at the ANU School of Economics and Finance.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}}
